2f94d24430b96ef64a259f6f2242592c8a00004b.summary: Commentary on the Ryuk ransomware, which the report says appeared in 2018, often distributed by commodity tools such as TrickBot. It describes human-operated attacks: tailored phishing, living off the land, credential theft with Mimikatz and Cobalt Strike, and Kerberoasting, Pass-the-Hash and Golden Ticket abuse to reach domain admin. It relays a claim that Ryuk operators are hiring. It says healthcare is heavily hit and recommends retiring NTLM and validating Kerberos.

2f2ce2648341ba5a21d599676e16dd5855a2d055.summary: Statement by the Department of Justice (spokesman Marc Raimondi) on the SolarWinds incident. On Dec. 24, 2020, the department's Office of the Chief Information Officer learned of previously unknown malicious activity involving access to its Microsoft O365 email environment. The access method was eliminated. Potentially accessed mailboxes appear limited to around 3 percent, and no classified systems are indicated as impacted. The activity was determined to be a major incident under FISMA. The statement was published 2021-01-06.

2f159048db296cab9486e7a29595398e82453fb0.summary: BleepingComputer reports an FBI FLASH alert on FIN7 sending malicious USB drives by mail via USPS to retail, restaurant and hotel businesses, targeting HR, IT and executive staff. The USB devices act as keyboards to launch PowerShell commands that fetch GRIFFON malware. Trustwave analysed one incident. Tools named include Metasploit, Cobalt Strike, Carbanak and Boostwrite.
